high.title: More than 20 banks simultaneously cut interest rates: Agribank, Vietcombank, VietinBank, BIDV and many major banks all join in
high.summary: Over 20 major Vietnamese banks have coordinated deposit rate cuts following a meeting between the State Bank of Vietnam and commercial banks on April 9th. The cuts range from 0.1-0.5% annually, with some banks like LPBank implementing the largest reduction of 1% for 36-60 month terms. Major state-owned banks including Vietcombank, VietinBank, BIDV, and Agribank all reduced rates by 0.5% for terms of 24+ months. This synchronized monetary easing signals SBV's coordination to support economic growth targets and reduce funding costs. For VND traders, this should weaken deposit demand and potentially pressure the VND. Bond yields may decline as banks seek alternative investments, while lower rates should boost economic activity and equity markets.

high.title: Securities market receives "dual boost", VN-Index expected to head towards 1,770 points
high.summary: MB Securities reports the Vietnamese stock market is receiving a "dual boost" from international factors (US-Iran ceasefire reducing geopolitical risks and global stock surge) and domestic factors (high-level personnel appointments, FTSE upgrade, and 17 banks cutting interest rates by up to 1% annually after the SBV meeting). The VN-Index has successfully formed a double bottom around the MA200 level and is expected to target 1,770 points. However, the market will face challenges in the 1,760-1,770 zone. This coordinated rate cutting cycle following SBV guidance represents a significant monetary policy shift that should support both equity valuations and economic growth while potentially weakening VND and lowering government bond yields.

high.title: FTSE Representative: Billions of USD about to flow into Vietnam and no more "hit and run"
high.summary: FTSE Russell's Asia-Pacific Policy Director Wanming Du confirms Vietnam has fully met criteria for Secondary Emerging Market status upgrade, expected around September 2026. The transition will occur gradually over 4 quarters rather than immediately, ensuring operational stability and liquidity. This measured approach addresses concerns about sudden capital flow surges and "hit and run" investment behavior. The upgrade represents billions of USD in structural capital inflows over time as Vietnam gains inclusion in major emerging market indices. For VND/USD, this suggests sustained foreign currency inflows that should strengthen the VND over time. Government bond yields may compress as foreign demand increases, while equity markets gain permanent institutional capital base rather than volatile speculative flows.

medium.title: One real estate stock faces risk of removal from VNDiamond basket
medium.summary: BIDV Securities forecasts KDH (Nha Khang Dien) faces removal risk from VN-Diamond Index due to insufficient foreign ownership limit maintenance below 65% minimum. Over 4 million KDH shares may be sold by ETFs, while other stocks like FPT, MBB, and TCB are expected to see increased weightings and ETF buying.

medium.title: Another 2 entities apply for gold bar production and gold import licenses, SBV is considering
medium.summary: Total applications for gold bar production and raw gold import licenses has reached 11 entities. SBV is coordinating with relevant ministries to review applications, with licensing process requiring close cooperation between agencies to ensure transparency and regulatory compliance.

medium.title: April 14: Gold bar and plain ring prices rise simultaneously
medium.summary: SJC gold prices increased by 1.5 million VND/tael to 170.0-173.0 million VND/tael by afternoon trading, with gold rings following similar increases. International gold maintained around $4,730-4,750/ounce after recovering above $4,700.

medium.title: One Vietnamese bank increases average employee income to over 900 million VND in 1 year
medium.summary: HSBC Vietnam reported 2025 results with total assets of 141 trillion VND (+3.2%), loans up 8.3% to 74.6 trillion VND, but pre-tax profit fell 6.9% to 4.141 trillion VND, the lowest in 4 years.

medium.title: International expert's view on concerns about market dependence on "Vingroup family" stocks
medium.summary: UBS's David Rabinowitz notes market concentration in Vingroup stocks is not unique to Vietnam but a global phenomenon. FTSE indices already calculate and control for concentration risk, with financial sector currently accounting for about 27% of index weighting.
